title: Why Does a Bugatti Need 10 Radiators?
description:
Your car has one radiator. The Bugatti Veyron has ten. Not because Bugatti wanted to show off, but because a car that makes more than one thousand horsepower turns a huge amount of fuel into heat, and that heat has to go somewhere, or the car destroys itself in minutes. Today, ten parts of a Bugatti that exist because of one crazy goal, and why each one exists.

Machine Reverse takes apart the machines you see every day and explains, part by part, why each one exists. This video covers 10 parts.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:10 1. The ten radiators
2:31 2. The W16 engine
3:53 3. The four turbochargers
5:07 4. The roof intakes
6:14 5. The airbrake wing
7:19 6. The fuel tank
8:34 7. The horseshoe grille
9:47 8. The C line
10:55 9. The gearbox
12:10 10. The test track
13:27 The verdict

Sources:
- Bugatti Veyron: ten radiators, W16, quad turbos, airbrake, fuel use at top speed, Ricardo gearbox: Wikipedia, "Bugatti Veyron" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bugatti_Veyron
- Bugatti Chiron: sequential turbos, C-line air intake, 490 km/h run at Ehra-Lessien (2019): Wikipedia, "Bugatti Chiron" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bugatti_Chiron
- W16 engine and the VR6 origin: Wikipedia, "W16 engine" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W16_engine
- Ehra-Lessien test track: Wikipedia, "Ehra-Lessien" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ehra-Lessien
- Ettore Bugatti and the horseshoe radiator, Type 35: Wikipedia, "Bugatti Type 35" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bugatti_Type_35
- Engine air consumption figures: Bugatti Newsroom https://newsroom.bugatti/
